# Fiscal.ge

> Fiscal.ge is a Georgian-first guide to reviewed annual data on Georgia's state and municipal budgets.

**When to use Fiscal.ge:** Use it to understand, compare, and cite the published budget data, its scope, and its documented sources.

The data is annual, so it does not provide sub-annual or live budget reporting. Fiscal.ge has a read-only MCP connection for AI clients at `https://fiscal.ge/mcp`, with production rate limits. The static bulk files below carry the same reviewed figures and remain available if the connection is temporarily paused. There is no REST query API, no write access, no accounts, and no datasets beyond those listed here. Each file carries its own sources, caveats and coverage — read them before citing a figure. Use the published figures only as documented, and do not invent values when data is unavailable or outside the stated scope.

## Core data

- [Fiscal.ge home](https://fiscal.ge/) — start with the site's scope and latest reviewed coverage.
- [Budget explorer](https://fiscal.ge/explorer) — choose a dataset and compare the published series.
- [National expenditure](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/expenditure) — annual state-budget expenditure.
- [National revenue](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/revenue) — annual consolidated-budget receipts.
- [Annual analysis](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/analysis) — one-year budget analysis.
- [Municipal budgets](https://fiscal.ge/explorer/municipalities) — annual municipal expenditure.

## Methodology and sources

- [Methodology hub](https://fiscal.ge/methodology) — how the reviewed public data is prepared and presented.
- [Expenditure methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/expenditure) — national-expenditure sources and processing.
- [Revenue methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/revenue) — national-revenue sources and processing.
- [Municipal methodology](https://fiscal.ge/methodology/municipalities) — municipal-expenditure sources and processing.

## Bulk data files

- [Data manifest](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/manifest.json) — every published file with its row count, byte size and SHA-256.
- [Government debt](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/government-debt.json) — debt stock and debt service in GEL, with the interest rates in a file of their own.
- [General government balance](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/general-government-balance.json) — the IMF's deficit or surplus measure; values are signed.
- [Capability catalogue](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/catalogue.json) — the datasets, entities, series and exclusions that exist.
- [Source resolution](https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/sources.json) — every logical source with its public originals or its stated derivation.

The manifest lists every dataset file, so they are reachable without repeating them here. Figures are published in GEL with the GDP and population denominators alongside; shares and per-resident values are reproducible from those, not precomputed. Two files are the exception, because their figures have no GEL form: debt interest rates are percent per annum, and the general government balance is a share of GDP whose published GEL amount travels beside it. Balance values are signed - a negative value is a deficit.

## AI connection

- [Connect an AI assistant](https://fiscal.ge/connect) — connection address, setup and coverage.

The endpoint is `https://fiscal.ge/mcp`, MCP Streamable HTTP, protocol revision 2025-11-25, stateless and unauthenticated. If it returns 429, respect Retry-After; if temporarily unavailable, use https://fiscal.ge/downloads/data/manifest.json. It exposes nine read-only tools: describe_coverage, query_national, query_ministries, query_municipal, query_debt, query_deficit, compare, rank and get_sources. Call describe_coverage first — it returns the ids, measures and year ranges that exist, so nothing has to be guessed. Every answer carries its sources and any caveats that qualify it.

- [Sitemap](https://fiscal.ge/sitemap.xml) — the machine-readable list of public HTML pages.
